_comments: The Sales API surface, declared as metadata. CodeGen reads these rows and emits one typed
a browser-safe package, which is the whole point: the client imports the CONTRACT without pulling
the server engine in behind it.
GenerationType=Manual, so CodeGen emits a typed SHELL and a hand-authored server subclass in
packages/CoreEntitiesServer supplies InternalExecute and registers under the operation key. The
server subclass registers LAST (it extends the generated base), so it wins ClassFactory dispatch.
AI generation is deliberately not used: this body orchestrates a multi-table transaction where
being subtly wrong produces a numbered deal with nothing under it — the exact failure the
KNOWN NOISE, inherited from the same CodeGen behaviour orders documents: remote operations carry
no schema, so CodeGen has no core/non-core partition for them the way it does for entities. The
configured target therefore receives the FULL operation set and this app's generated file also
picks up MJ's own core operations. Harmless — they are all GenerationType=Manual, which emits an
unregistered type shell: dead exported interfaces, no @RegisterClass, no runtime effect.

fields.Name: Save Deal
fields.Description: Create or update a deal together with its lines and its negotiated payment schedule, in ONE transaction. This is the operation that makes browser-side deal entry possible at all: a browser holds the generated DealEntity rather than DealEntityServer, so line and schedule collections are transient properties on the server entity and cannot cross the entity-save boundary as scalars. Saving the header and then each child as separate round trips is the alternative, and a failure partway through it leaves a numbered deal with nothing under it. Prices nothing — every figure it accepts is either an INPUT to the pricing engine or a transcription of what was signed.
